churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is properly centralized and no framework internals are relied on, so an adapter or Hono upgrade would touch almost nothing. But the codebase is entirely untyped, keeps a dead duplicate of its route logic, and sprinkles manual escaping and htmx magic strings across files — the kind of low-level coupling that generates churn as the app grows.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled HTML escaping with a custom escapeHtml that must be remembered at every interpolation (~40 call sites); a single omission is an XSS vulnerability.
findings.suggestion: Use hono/html's `html` tagged template (auto-escapes by default, `raw` for trusted fragments) or hono/jsx components — both are current, supported primitives that remove the escape-or-forget decision.

findings.issue: Upstream fetch has no timeout or AbortController; a hung PokeAPI connection stalls the corresponding request and its shared pending-promise entry indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Use AbortSignal.timeout(...) (or an AbortController with a cleanup) in fetchJson so failures surface and the pending cache entry is released.

findings.issue: renderMovePageByName, renderAbilityPageByName and renderTypePageByName are exported but never used; they duplicate the fetch+404 logic already in server.mjs routes.
findings.suggestion: Delete them, or make them the single implementation the routes call.

findings.issue: Static assets are hand-served via fs.readFileSync into memory with a custom readPublicFile/fallback helper, re-implementing what the Node adapter provides.
findings.suggestion: Use serveStatic from '@hono/node-server' (with the build script's copied public/ dir), or at minimum drop the require.resolve fallback duplicated in build.mjs:12.

findings.issue: htmx partial rendering is detected by header sniffing repeated in each route, with target ids ('pokemon-results', 'moves') stringly coupled to the view templates.
findings.suggestion: Extract one helper (e.g. isPartial(c, target)) and define the target ids as shared constants imported by both server and views.

findings.issue: Zero TypeScript in a Hono app with a large external API surface; Hono's typed-route/typed-handler facilities are unused and PokeAPI shape drift is caught only at request time.
findings.suggestion: Even without a full migration, add a few interfaces for the API resources in api.mjs (Species, Pokemon, Move, Ability, Type) to make the boundary explicit.

summary: This app will age well at the dependency level: hono, @hono/node-server and htmx are pinned to the exact latest stable releases (verified against npm/GitHub, Oct 2026), the router/adapter/htmx APIs used are all current, and every upstream data access is isolated in one well-designed module. The forward-looking weaknesses are in the view layer and typing: a hand-rolled escape function instead of hono/html or hono/jsx, dead duplicated route helpers, untyped PokeAPI data, and a fetch with no timeout. Solid 4 — nothing legacy, a few avoidable maintenance risks.
